newsitem.title: USA: Deutsche to open US junk-bond shop in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche to open US junk-bond shop in 1997.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell plans to enter the U.S. junk bond business in 1997 and is currently in the initial phase of putting a sales, trading and research team together, said a source close to the situation.
The source said Deutsche plans to build a high-yield shop slowly, as the firm is mindful of the fact that spreads are extremely tight in the marketplace.
Deutsche hopes to make its first individual hires over the next several months and has narrowed down a short-list of candidates, he said.
He said Deutsche will not hire a team of people, but expects to bring on staffers one-by-one.
A Deutsche spokeswoman confirmed the firm has had long-term interest in high-yield but would not comment on any hiring plans.
The source said Deutsche always intended to get into the high-yield business but first wanted to establish itself as a player in more liquid markets.
Over the course of 1996, Deutsche built sales, trading and research departments in the North American government bond, mortgage-backed securities and high-grade corporate bond markets.
The firm hired top-flight Wall Street talent including Paul Jacobson, formerly a partner at Goldman Sachs & Co, who currently serves as head of fixed-income trading.
Jacobson and Grant Kvalheim, head of debt capital markets, have been spearheading Deutsche's hiring for fixed income in the U.S.
Calls to Jacobson were not immediately returned. Kvalheim was not immediately available for comment.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell is the investment banking and securities subsidiary of Deutsche Bank AG.
Deutsche will be the latest of a string of financial firms to get into the high-yield business. Other recent entrants include Montgomery Securities and BankBoston.
High-yield bond issuance in the U.S. came close to record levels in 1996, totalling $70.8 billion. Analysts note junk bonds are currently trading at historically tight spread levels.
